checks: Injectivity and the exact pushforward give |T(B_r(x))|=|B_r(x)| for interior closed balls whose images are compact. Differentiability bounds the image in a small thickening of the derivative ellipsoid and thus forces |det DT|≥1, excluding a singular derivative.

The derivative is symmetric positive semidefinite, so the determinant of (1−θ)I+θDT is at least (det DT)^θ≥1 by multiplying the scalar arithmetic–geometric means. Monotonicity makes S strongly monotone with constant 1−θ and its inverse Lipschitz on the image.

The Lipschitz inverse takes null subsets of the image to null sets. Differentiability and the inverse Lipschitz estimate bound each small output ball's preimage at an interior image point by the inverse derivative ellipsoid with radius r+o(r), so its density is at most one. The interior image is σ-compact and carries all input volume.

The two θ values send base -k,k+1 to exactly 0,1 and true convex compatibility gives S(A)⊂B. On a product with B=-B the reflection interpolants are the two signed scalings by 1/(2k+1), giving densities (2k+1)^d on positive-volume images.
The cited source §4 includes the same specified interpolation claim and nonmonotone counterexample.

overlap.comparison: The accepted transport theorem constructs one triangular coupling with the optimal density ceiling, including unit mass-volume interpolation in the equal-volume case. The present claim applies to an externally specified monotone differentiable map and supplies a nonmonotone counterexample.

This accepted result is an existence theorem for a suitable multiway law at an actual integer barycentric target. It neither constrains a specified endpoint map nor implies that arbitrary volume-preserving maps have a bounded interpolant.

summary: The specified-map hypotheses yield a unit-density interpolation law on both true target fibers, and the reflection map verifies the failure under mere volume preservation.
